First gun I highly recommend a .22 either pistol or rifle.

Some considerations you might not have considered is that ammo can get very expensive. .25 cents a round doesn't sound like a lot at first but consider that a 30 round magazine will hold $7.50 in ammo. And you're not going to just shoot 1 magazine each time you go out. I've burned through $200 bucks in one outing and I know others must have done more. And .25 cents is on the lower side of how much .223/5.56 ammo can go for. And to get the lower price you sometimes have to buy in bulk like 200 rounds +. Not all the time but it's not unusual to see sales for 20 cent ammo in packs of 500 or something online without factoring shipping.

Another thing you need to consider is if you actually have a range or place to shoot a rifle. I mean something with some distance, at least 100 yards and ideally even more. I say this because I live in the city. To get to a place to shoot for free on public land it's about an hour drive each way and it's almost always crowded on the weekends when it's nice. And those places don't even go out to 100 yards, I think maybe 90 yards at one part. It really makes no sense to practice there with a high powered scoped rifle but rather just to plink and maybe half seriously dick around. Ranges exist but they charge dues, have wait lists months long, and/or require an already established member to vouch for you. How frequently you shoot will dictate if getting a range membership will be worth it. And if you got into reloaded it will help offset ammo costs but only after you pay off the initial startup costs.

Now I'm not saying any of this applies to you. I know for a fact there's TON of shooters in the country that don't have to deal with this. They know someone with land or live in a rural enough area where it's only a 20 min drive to places you can shoot out to 500 yards or more. You might know someone that's a range member already. The ranges by you don't require memberships and just charge a modest flat fee. Or a million other things. But it's really something you should take a look into before handing over a big wad of cash.

Let's go with a conservative approach and say you do have someplace to go about 30 minutes away to shoot for free but it only goes out to 50 yards and maybe one or two ranges nearby BUT they only go out to 100 yards. Take this into account when you get/build your rifle. If this were the case you wouldn't be putting a powerful scope on it (which can cost as much as the rifle itself). But open sights or something like an eotech or red dot would be perfect.

So why the .22? Easy to find ammo (barring shortages). Cheap ammo. Incredibly fun. Easy to resell if you decide it's not for you. Even experienced gun owners owns at least one. Everyone love theirs. Many of them you can mod the crap out of. Affordable. Perfect to use to introduce new shooters to if you bring along nogunz friends. Can take small game. If you do your part it can be used for self defense. You can shoot it all day. You're going to get one anyway if you're like the other 99% of us.
